'''''Nepeta racemosa''''', the '''dwarf catnip'''<ref name = RHSPF/> or '''raceme catnip''', [[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''N. mussiniii'',<ref name = TPL>{{cite web | url= http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-134920 | title= ''Nepeta racemosa'' | publisher= The Plant List | access-date = 11 April 2018}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the mint [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Lamiaceae, [[native plant|native]] to the Caucasus, Turkey and northern Iran. Growing to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide, it is a [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] with aromatic leaves and violet or lilac-blue flowers in summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

This plant is one of several ''Nepeta'' species to be cultivated as an ornamental. It is particularly suitable for the front of a flower border or as [[groundcover]]. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]],<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Nepeta racemosa''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/68135/Nepeta-racemosa/Details |access-date=12 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 66 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 12 April 2018}}</ref> as has the [[cultivar]] ‘Walker’s Low’<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/55055/Nepeta-racemosa-Walker-s-Low/Details |title = ''Nepeta racemosa'' 'Walker's Low'|access-date=12 February 2020}}</ref>

Nepetas are notable for their euphoric effect on some domestic cats. It is thought to be caused by the chemical [[nepetalactone]] which also has effects on some insects, repelling cockroaches and mosquitoes.

==Taxonomy==
''Nepeta racemosa'' is classified in the genus ''[[Nepeta]]'' in the [[Lamiaceae]]. It has three [[subspecies]]. It was scientifically described and named by [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] in 1785.<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id=452683-1 |title=''Nepeta racemosa'' Lam. |access-date=18 December 2024}}</ref>

===Names===
The Latin [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''racemosa'' means “having [[raceme]]s of flowers”.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref>
